cleanIntro: The P-07 is CZ's polymer-framed, hammer-fired compact, and its defining feature is that the thumb safety and the decocking element are interchangeable — the same pistol can be either, and CZ publishes the swap. That means two operating sections of the book explicitly exclude one another and you have to know which one your gun is. The strip is CZ 75 in shape but simpler: half-cock, line up the guidelines, tap the slide stop out from the right. Everything below is read off the English section of CZ's P-07 manual, PDF pages 2 to 15.

steps.title: Safety or decocker — and it can be changed, so check the gun not the box
steps.action: Look at the control above the grip on the left side. A lever that stays up with a red dot beneath it is a manual safety; one that springs back after being pushed down is a decocking element. The P-07 is designed so these can be swapped, so do not assume the pistol still has what it left the factory with.
steps.prose: This is the one CZ design where the safety fit is genuinely a user-changeable state rather than a model number, and CZ describes the exchange in the maintenance section. It matters here because two operating sections of this book are written to exclude one another on exactly this point, and because the decocking build needs a control-element spring that the safety build does not. Read your own pistol before you read any operating instruction.
steps.quote: Mutual interchangeability of the safety and hammer decocking element
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Pistol Description and Terminology — characteristic features, p.5

steps.title: The safety section is written to exclude the decocker guns
steps.action: If your P-07 has a manual safety, this is your section: with the hammer cocked, push the safety up until the red warning dot is covered, which blocks the trigger mechanism and the slide. If your P-07 has a decocking element, this section does not apply to it.
steps.prose: CZ prints the exclusion as the first line under the heading. The reason is a real hazard, not tidiness: on a P-07 the safety lever CAN be pushed to Safe with the hammer resting on the safety notch, and CZ warns that forcing the hammer back or pulling the trigger from that state could damage the trigger mechanism and cause unwanted firing even with the safety apparently locked. So the safety is engaged with the hammer fully cocked and at no other time, which makes it a short-interruption device rather than a way to store the gun.
steps.quote: The version equipped with a decocking device is not covered in this section!
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Engaging the Safety Mode, opening line, p.8
steps.warn: CZ's own words on this pistol: the safety shall only be engaged with the hammer in its rear position, i.e. cocked, and the use of the safety is convenient for short interruptions of firing only.

steps.title: And the decocking section excludes the manual-safety guns
steps.action: If your P-07 has a decocking element, point it in a safe direction and thumb the decocking control lever down; the hammer lowers from cocked to the safety notch with no need to touch the trigger. If your P-07 has a manual safety, this section does not apply to it.
steps.prose: The mirror-image exclusion heads the decocking section. On the decocker build the hammer comes down mechanically and the P-07's firing pin safety keeps the pin blocked while it does, leaving the pistol safe to handle and ready to fire double action. On the manual-safety build there is no such lever, and lowering the hammer means thumb on the hammer with the trigger pulled over whatever is in the chamber. Applying the wrong section's method is precisely what these two sentences exist to prevent.
steps.quote: The version equipped with a manual safety is not covered in this section!
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Decocking, opening line, p.8

steps.title: Check the chambering — the .380 P-07 is a different action
steps.action: Read the caliber marking on the barrel or slide. A 9x19 P-07 is a short-recoil locked-breech pistol. The 9 mm Browning (.380) version is not: it is a blowback, with no barrel locking action at all.
steps.prose: This changes what you are looking at when the slide comes off and what fouls where. A locked-breech P-07 has a barrel that tilts and a lower lug the slide stop shaft passes through; the blowback .380 does not lock and its recoil spring is doing the whole job of holding the breech shut. Fouling and wear patterns differ accordingly, and so does what a worn recoil spring means. It is one sentence in the description section and it is easy to read past.
steps.aside: The same book also references a CZ P-07 pistol in calibre .22 LR. Confirm the caliber marking on your own pistol rather than assuming from the frame.
steps.quote: The 9 mm Browning (.380) version is equipped with blowback breech.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Pistol Description and Terminology, p.5

steps.title: Magazine out, then the chamber checked by eye
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Depress the magazine catch with the thumb or middle finger and let the magazine fall clear. Draw the slide back and confirm the last cartridge has been extracted and ejected, let the slide run fully forward, then dry-fire into a safe area.
steps.prose: The P-07's magazine catch is the reversible user type and can be set up by a gunsmith for either hand, so where it sits is a property of your gun rather than of the model. CZ makes the empty magazine well a precondition of disassembly and states it as its own numbered step. The P-07 has no loaded chamber indicator, so the chamber gets looked at rather than inferred — the hammer position tells you nothing about whether the chamber is full.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the magazine. The pistol must not be disassembled with the magazine inserted!
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 1, p.9
steps.warn: MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER — CZ prints this as the third numbered step of the strip, in capitals.

steps.title: Leave the back strap pin alone — that one is a gunsmith's
steps.action: Do not remove the back strap insert as part of cleaning. On the P-07 the back strap is retained by the main spring plug pin, and that pin holds a compressed main spring behind it. CZ says to entrust the task to a gunsmith.
steps.prose: This is the P-07 trap and it is worth calling out because the same job on a P-10 is a simple roll pin. Here the pin doing the retaining is also the one containing the main spring, so drifting it out on the bench releases a spring under load into your hand. The grip inserts come off many polymer pistols during a clean; on this one they do not. Wipe the back strap in place instead.
steps.quote: In order to change the back strap inserts it is necessary to remove the main spring plug pin. To avoid injuries be very careful when removing the pin as it secures the main spring plug as well as the compressed main spring. Entrust the task to a gunsmith.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — Changing the Back Strap Inserts, p.9

steps.title: Safety OFF so the slide will move, hammer down to half-cock
steps.action: Put the safety to the "OFF" position to release the slide, then retract the hammer slightly and let it back down until it stops on the half-cock (safety) notch.
steps.prose: On a manual-safety P-07 the safety blocks the slide as well as the trigger, so a slide that will not move is the safety still standing up rather than a fault; on a decocker P-07 there is nothing to switch and the slide is free from the start. Half-cock then parks the hammer clear of the firing pin and out of the slide's way, which is what the next step needs — with the hammer fully down the slide has to shove it back, and with the hammer cocked the mainspring pushes against your grip. A small distinct catch is the confirmation it has seated.
steps.quote: 2. Put the safety to "OFF" position, in order to release the movement of the slide.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, p.9

steps.title: Slide back until the guidelines line up — against the retracted hammer
steps.action: Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and grip the top of the front of the slide firmly. Push the slide slightly rearward until the rear of the slide is against the retracted hammer and the guidelines on the frame and the slide are in line.
steps.prose: The P-07 gives you two references at once and they are meant to agree: the slide's rear comes up against the half-cocked hammer, and at that same point the scribed guidelines on frame and slide sit in register. If the hammer is fully down the slide travels past the index; if it is fully cocked, the slide meets it too early. When both cues agree you are at the one position where the slide stop's shaft is clear of the barrel's lower lug.
steps.quote: 6. Push the slide slightly rearwards until the rear of the slide is against the retracted hammer and the guidelines on the frame and the slide are in line.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, p.9

steps.title: Tap the slide stop from the right, withdraw it from the left
steps.action: Holding the guidelines in register, tap the protruding slide stop shaft from the RIGHT side of the pistol — the magazine base works as the drift — then pull the slide stop out from the LEFT.
steps.prose: One direction only, and only at the indexed position. If it does not start under a tap, the slide has drifted off the guidelines; reset it rather than hitting harder, because the shaft bears on the barrel's lower lug and heavy blows peen it. Keep a firm grip on the slide the whole time — the instant the stop clears, the recoil spring is free to push the slide forward off the frame. Using the magazine base rather than a steel punch keeps the stop's head unmarked.
steps.quote: 7. Push (tap) the slide stop from the right hand side of the weapon, i.e. using the magazine base (Fig. 8). Remove the slide stop from the left.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 7, p.9

steps.title: Slide and barrel forward off the frame
steps.action: Draw the slide with the barrel still inside it forward off the front of the frame, supporting both as they leave the rails.
steps.prose: The P-07 runs its slide on short steel inserts moulded into the polymer frame rather than on full-length rails, so it comes off easily but the inserts are the part to look after — keep the slide square and let it travel straight forward rather than levering one end up. It stays under recoil spring tension the whole way, so do not let go halfway. Once clear you are holding slide, barrel and recoil spring together as a unit.
steps.quote: 8. Pull the slide and the barrel forward off the frame.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 8, p.9

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel
steps.action: Invert the slide, lift the recoil spring assembly out at the muzzle end easing the tension off as it comes, then lift the barrel free of the slide.
steps.prose: That order is fixed by the geometry — the recoil spring bears on the barrel, so the barrel will not lift while the spring is in. Take the spring out with a hand at each end; on a compact pistol it is short and stiff and will jump if released at an angle. With both out you are looking at the four pieces this procedure yields: frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring, with the magazine already aside.
steps.quote: 9. Remove the recoil spring and finally the barrel.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, step 9, p.9

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring, with the slide stop and magazine set aside. That is the whole field strip CZ publishes for the P-07 — the firing pin, extractor, hammer, sear, back strap and the safety or decocking element all stay in the pistol for routine work.
steps.prose: Those pieces reach everything the cleaning section asks for: bore and chamber from the breech end, the breech face and extractor claw, the inside of the slide and the frame's rail inserts, and the whole outside of the barrel including the lower lug. CZ's closing note is that routine maintenance needs nothing further, and that firing pin cleaning is a gunsmith's job. The two things the book does hand you beyond this are stripping the magazine and — uniquely for a CZ — exchanging the control element.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges has been fired, it is advisable to also disassemble magazine and to entrust the pistol to a competent gunsmith for the firing pin cleaning.
steps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping for Cleaning, closing note, p.10

deepSteps.title: Magazine base — read the lock design before you push
deepSteps.action: If the magazine base has a hole, push the base lock through it and slide the base slightly forward. If the rear of the magazine carries a sliding base lock, move it to its disassembly position first and then slide the base forward.
deepSteps.prose: CZ builds both patterns across the P-07 range and they do not respond to the same technique — a punch used on a sliding-lock magazine only marks the polymer. Identify yours, then move the base only as far as it takes to clear the lock; the base is still on its guide rails at that point, which is where you want it with a compressed spring underneath. This job is the one CZ names for the owner after a heavy session, and on a carry P-07 the magazine collects pocket lint faster than the pistol collects carbon.
deepSteps.quote: There is a difference depending on the magazine design. If there is a hole in the magazine base, push the base lock through the hole and slide the base slightly forward.
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Thumb on the base as it leaves the rails
deepSteps.action: Cover the base with your thumb to hold the spring, then use the other hand to slide the base completely out of its guiding rails. Let your thumb up slowly so the spring rises under control.
deepSteps.prose: The base is the only thing containing a compressed magazine spring, and released without a thumb on it the base, spring and follower leave together. Do it over a bench with the magazine mouth pointed away from your face. Note which way up the follower sits as it comes out — it is handed, and one refitted upside down presents the first round nose-high and will stop the pistol on the first shot.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the base with your thumb to hold the spring and use the other hand to slide the base completely out of its guiding rails. Be careful during the disassembly as the spring could fly out, or even cause an injury.
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Magazine Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Exchanging the control element — the ejector and trigger bar come first
deepSteps.action: If you are converting between safety and decocker, the LEFT element comes out only after the ejector is depressed downward, and the RIGHT element goes in only after the trigger bar is depressed downward. No special tooling is required.
deepSteps.prose: This is the P-07's signature job and it is a sequence, not a knack: each side is blocked by a different internal part, so pressing the wrong one gets you nowhere and levering gets you a bent trigger bar. The configurations are not symmetrical either — the safety build installs safeties only, while the decocker build additionally needs the control element spring fitted with its shorter end supported by the nose of the control element body and the opposite end in the pin hollow. Get that spring wrong and the decocker will not return.
deepSteps.quote: The left safety or left decocking element can be removed first after depressing the ejector downward. Before assembling the right safety or right decocking element it is necessary to depress the trigger bar downward.
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Exchange of Control Elements, p.10
deepSteps.warn: CZ recommends being trained in this exchange under the supervision of an experienced gunsmith, or following the guidance on the manufacturer's website, rather than working it out on the bench.

deepSteps.title: Reassemble, then stop
deepSteps.action: Wipe the magazine body inside, the follower and the spring dry — no oil in the body — and put the magazine back together. Go no further into the pistol.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside a magazine holds grit against the case walls and slows the follower, which on a carried P-07 shows up as a sluggish last round rather than an obvious stoppage. While it is apart, sight along the feed lips against a known-good magazine; a spread lip is a magazine to retire, not to bend back. Beyond the magazine and the control element, CZ's instruction is that the pistol goes to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended. Should your pistol require adjustment or repair be sure the task is entrusted to a competent gunsmith!
deepSteps.cite: CZ P-07 — INSTRUCTION MANUAL / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — CAUTION following Exchange of Control Elements, p.10

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean patch on the rod through bore and chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean — enough on its own if the P-07 has fired only a few rounds
For a heavily fouled bore, brush gun cleaning solution in, let it act about 10 minutes, then scrub the bore out thoroughly
Rod and brush enter from the CHAMBER end and the brush is pushed right out of the muzzle before reversing; reversing inside a short compact barrel is how a brush sticks
Dry bore and chamber with a clean patch and confirm all powder residue and fouling is gone

cleaning.name: SLIDE, RAILS & BARREL EXTERIOR
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, brass bristle brush or wooden scraper on the breech face, the extractor and its cut, and the inside of the slide
Clean the steel rail inserts moulded into the polymer frame and the recesses around them — that is where a carried P-07 collects lint and grit
Wipe the outside of the barrel including the lower lug the slide stop shaft bears on, and check that lug for peening
Preserving oil or paraffin oil may be used here — NEVER the agent designed for barrel bore cleaning, which stays in the joints and corrodes them later
Check that no cloth particles or brush bristles are lodged in any part of the pistol

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: With bore, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or apply it as a spray, then remove all excess
At very low temperatures take the oil off all accessible parts or use a lubricant prepared for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in a demanding climate only and must be removed thoroughly from every part before use
Wipe the barrel bore dry before shooting

reassembly: Barrel into the inverted slide first, then the recoil spring seated on the barrel — the spring will not sit right if the barrel is not fully home.
Run the slide onto the frame from the front and push it back until the guidelines on frame and slide are in register with the slide's rear against the retracted hammer.
Insert the slide stop from the LEFT and press it home flush on the right; thumb pressure is enough at the indexed position.
Let the slide run forward, cycle it once by hand, and confirm the slide stop has stayed seated.
Dry-patch the bore before the pistol is carried or fired.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty. On a manual-safety P-07: with the hammer cocked the safety should go up and block both trigger and slide — and do not test it from half-cock, because CZ warns that forcing the hammer or the trigger from that state can damage the trigger mechanism. On a decocker P-07: the lever should lower the hammer to the safety notch without the trigger moving and spring back up on its own. On either build the hammer should catch cleanly at half-cock and sit clear of the firing pin, the firing pin should stay blocked with the trigger untouched, the slide stop should sit flush after a hand cycle, and an empty magazine should lock the slide back.
